newsitem.title: LATVIA: DECISION REACHED TO COVER LATAVIO DEBTS - REPORT.
newsitem.headline: DECISION REACHED TO COVER LATAVIO DEBTS - REPORT.

text.p: Latvia has decided to cover in full the debts of Latavio, the bankrupt national air carrier, to Russia, in order to lift the ban on airBaltic's Russian flights, the Diena newspaper said on Wednesday.

Latavio's debt to Russia's Aeroflot and Moscow airport, worth $2.8 million, has been cited by Russian officials as a reason for refusing airBaltic, part-owned by Sandinavian Airlines (SAS), flying rights to destinations in Russia, the newspaper writes.
Latvia earlier said it was ready to pay the debt but was unwilling to link it to the flying rights issue.
"The debt will be paid by the Latvian Privatisation Agency (LPA), Latvijas Gaisa satiksme agency and Riga airport," Talis Linkaitis, an LPA oficial, was quoted by Diena as saying.
